newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on CBOT, crushers, funds.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on CBOT, crushers, funds.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on the higher CBOT soycomplex, crusher and fund demand.

"Crushers bought 500 to 800 November, locals covered shorts," a trader said. "We had commercial and fund buying, locals took profits, there was a lack of hedges," a trader said. Nov-Jan spread at $4.10, Jan-Mar $1, Nov-May $6, Nov-Mar $5.30. Volume was heavy.
November canola rose $4.60 to $439.60, January up $4.10 to $443.40. November flax rose $2.50 to $372 on commission short covering. Feed peas did not trade.
Cargill sold October oats down US$3.60 to US$128.40.
October feed wheat rose $2.40 to $209.20, December up $0.20 to $192.70 on rail car allocation concerns nearby.
"The spreads are inverting sharply with Alberta Wheat Pool a scale up seller of the Oct-Mar spread," a trader said. Oct-Mar spread at $22, Oct-Dec at $17, Mar-May at even money.
November western barley lost $0.60 to $150.20, February down $0.60 to $154.20 on moderate hedges, commission selling met by commercial scale-down buying. Nov-Feb spread at $4.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
